title: Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: “Risk comes from not knowing what you are doing.”
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

book_paragraphs: TD Power Systems Limited designs and builds custom AC generators and industrial motors for global gas-turbine, steam, hydro, and engine OEMs. Between our 12 November 2026 baseline dossier and this 25 November 2026 refresh, the company delivered a sharp operational upgrade alongside a severe technical breakdown. On the 13 November Q2 FY2027 call, management raised FY2027 revenue guidance to ₹2,900–₹3,000 crore and set FY2028 guidance at ₹3,400–₹3,500 crore [40]. H1 consolidated operating cash flow rebounded to ₹211.74 crore (~101% of H1 PAT), and the firm broke ground on 19 November on a dedicated Siemens Energy fourth plant [42][46]. Even so, our price-blind business quality verdict stays CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (KPI health: PASS_WITH_WATCH). Export inflows (90–92% of H1) face 50% U.S. tariff and Turkey routing risks, standalone receivables jumped 35% in six months to ₹956.31 crore, the fourth plant uses single-OEM build-to-print IP, and QIP proceeds deployment remains undisclosed [42][44][46].

Our new-capital verdict is REJECTED (Conviction Tier: TIER_0; Rejection Reasons: TREND and VALUATION). On the 2026-11-23 NSE market-facts ledger cutoff, TDPOWERSYS closed at ₹605.30 in Stage 3. Two sessions later, on the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, it fell another 3.02% to ₹587.05. That drop broke below the 200-day SMA (₹601.31), S1 pivot (₹599.53), and 40-week EMA (₹608.25). The stock is now locked in STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, CAP_REJECTED). It trades 11.12% below its 10-week EMA, 17.39% below its 50-day SMA, and 11.84% below its 30-week SMA. It also logged 7 distribution days in 25 sessions, -40.04% 28-day relative strength versus the Nifty 50, and removal from TheWrap Stage 2 list. At 54.19x–55.7x trailing earnings, valuation leaves no margin of safety against institutional selling—evidenced by Oxbow Capital cutting its stake from 3.08% to 1.42% through 13 November [45].

Our existing holding action shifts from HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP to EXIT_ON_BOUNCE across all 470 Zerodha shares. On the 2026-11-23 positions ledger (priced at ₹605.30 NSE close), those 470 shares held a market value of ₹2,84,491.00 against a ₹2,99,162.95 cost basis (₹636.52 average cost). That equaled an unrealized loss of -₹14,671.95 (-4.90%) and a 6.67% portfolio weight. At the live 2026-11-25 close of ₹587.05, market value is ₹2,75,913.50 (-₹23,249.45 unrealized loss, -7.77%). Waiting for a ₹620 bounce across all 470 shares offers an unfavorable 0.78:1 bounce-versus-stop ratio (+₹32.95 upside vs -₹42.05 downside to ₹545) while carrying unhedged 6.56%-ATR gap risk. We therefore tighten the exit into two tranches. First, sell 235 shares (50%) immediately at market (~₹587.05) to halve Stage 4 weight from 6.67% to ~3.3%. Second, exit the remaining 235 shares into broken 200D/40W resistance at ₹601–₹615 (alert ₹605.00) or on a daily close below our upward-ratcheted ₹545.00 hard stop (up from ₹520.00).

Halving the position immediately cuts unhedged stop-gap dollar risk in half. On the residual 235 shares, a bounce to ₹605–₹615 recovers +₹4,218 to +₹6,568 versus ₹587.05, while the ratcheted ₹545.00 hard stop caps residual incremental downside at -7.16% (-₹9,882, or roughly -₹9,055 per 1-ATR gap). That protects the portfolio against an air-pocket drop toward the ₹485 S2 pivot or ₹410 bear case. Because TDPOWERSYS is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID (outside the NSE F&O segment), no listed puts or call spreads exist to hedge this risk. Cash-equity stop discipline is mandatory.

Our updated post-QIP valuation framework trims the FY29E Base value from ₹820 to ₹720 (₹16.00 FY29E diluted EPS at 45x P/E, 45% probability, stepping up from ₹14.75 FY28E midpoint EPS). We set Bear at ₹410 (₹11.70 EPS at 35x, 35% probability) and Bull at ₹990 (₹19.80 EPS at 50x, 20% probability). The probability-weighted fair value is ₹665.50 (~₹666). That offers just +13.4% upside from ₹587.05 against -30.2% bear-case downside. Even flawless delivery of FY2028 guidance (₹3,400–₹3,500 crore revenue, ~₹480 crore PAT) yields only ₹19,200 crore of equity value at 40x—flat with today's ₹19,457 crore TradingView market cap [40][42].

Across horizons, our judgments remain cleanly separated. Short-term trading and momentum is REJECTED / AVOID under Stage 4 supply dominance and weak 4-hour momentum (4H RSI 37.86, close below 4H EMA20 ₹620.33). Medium-term inflection is CONDITIONAL WATCH pending Q3/Q4 FY2027 execution, clean U.S. tariff and Turkey routing, and stable receivables. Long-term compounding remains POTENTIAL, NOT PROVEN. Expansion capex at the Siemens Energy fourth plant must prove high returns without repeated working-capital stretch or equity dilution [42][46].

Capital redeployment stays 100% in CASH once the 470-share exit executes (~₹1.38 lakh immediate on 235 shares + ~₹1.41–₹1.45 lakh on residual 235 shares into ₹601–₹615). We allocate 0% to the active India shortlist and 0% to outside candidates inside this single-company dossier. India's Nifty 50 regime remains in an Uptrend with narrow breadth (55.2% above 50DMA, 48.2% above 200DMA, 3 distribution days). However, electrical-equipment peers Cummins India and CG Power are also locked in Stage 4 markdowns. Holding cash preserves optionality until the next portfolio-level audit deploys into a confirmed Stage 2 pullback.

Four falsifiable checkpoints will govern any future re-underwriting. First, Q3 and Q4 FY2027 revenue must hit ₹725–₹750 crore per quarter at 18.5%–20% EBITDA margins. Second, audited FY2027 CFO must stay above 85%–90% of PAT while standalone receivables stop outpacing revenue. Third, management must disclose ₹675 crore equity-raise deployment and prove clean U.S. tariff and Turkey customs execution. Fourth, the weekly chart must form a Stage 1 base and break out into Stage 2 above rising 50-day and 200-day averages. Until those four gates clear, capital belongs in cash.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good companies can have bad stocks when high multiples collide with tariff risk, institutional selling, and Stage 4 technical damage. Separate operational admiration from portfolio risk management: reject new capital in Stage 4, halve the position immediately, ratchet the stop up to ₹545, and exit the residual tranche into broken 200D/40W resistance.
